title: Highest goodness is like water
shortSummary: The water metaphor connects benefiting things, non-contention and dwelling in low places as relational qualities.
curatorialDescription: The full sentence group is retained instead of extracting a four-character maxim.
researchNote: Variants and major commentaries on goodness, non-contention and low position remain to be added.

sources.title: Received editions and chapter references for the Daodejing
sources.locator: 第二十五章（“人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然”）
sources.role: Initial basis for the Daoist passage and chapter locator

profile.originalText: 上善若水。水善利万物而不争，处众人之所恶，故几于道。
profile.punctuatedText: 上善若水。水善利万物而不争，处众人之所恶，故几于道。
profile.modernZh: 最高的善像水：滋养万物而不争，处在众人不愿处的位置，所以接近于道。
profile.translationEn: Highest goodness is like water. Water benefits all things without contention and dwells where people dislike; thus it is close to the Dao.
